title: zk-SNARK execution proofs
description: zk-SNARKs prove 'this program ran correctly on these inputs' with a tiny proof anyone verifies in milliseconds — without revealing the inputs or the full trace. Systems like RISC Zero execute RISC-V programs and emit SNARKs of correct execution: verifiable compute with private data.
method: Compile the program to a zkVM circuit; execute, generating the proof; the verifier checks the proof against the claimed output.
usage: Use for outsourced compute on private data; verify proofs before accepting results.

demo.code:
print('program: tax_calc(private_income) -> $4,200')
print('proof: 2KB SNARK, verified in 8ms (income stays private)')

title: Binary transparency logs
description: Binary transparency (like Certificate Transparency for code) logs every released binary's hash in an append-only Merkle tree. Users verify their binary is in the log; monitors watch for unexpected entries. A compromised build server can't ship a targeted malicious binary silently — the log would show it.
method: Log each release hash in the Merkle tree; ship inclusion proofs with binaries; monitors alert on unrecognized entries.
usage: Log every release; verify inclusion on install; monitor the log for surprises.

demo.code:
print('release v2.4 hash logged: Merkle root r9f2')
print('install verifies inclusion proof -> binary is the logged one')

title: Control-flow integrity (CFI)
description: CFI enforces at runtime that indirect jumps only go to valid targets, defeating control-flow hijacks (ROP/JOP). Clang's CFI and Intel CET implement it with low overhead — integrity of the running program's control flow, checked on every indirect branch.
method: Build the valid-target graph; instrument indirect branches; violations trap; deploy on supported hardware/compilers.
usage: Enable CFI for C/C++ attack surface; treat violations as exploits in progress.

demo.code:
print('indirect call to 0x41414141 (not a valid target)')
print('CFI: TRAP — control-flow hijack blocked')

title: Proof-carrying build pipelines
description: The build pipeline itself emits integrity evidence: SBOMs, provenance attestations (SLSA), and step signatures. SLSA levels formalize this — level 3 requires hardened builders and non-falsifiable provenance. The artifact's history is as verifiable as the artifact.
method: Emit SLSA provenance per build; sign each pipeline step; verify provenance before deployment.
usage: Adopt SLSA progressively; gate deployments on provenance verification.

demo.code:
print('SLSA L3 provenance: builder hardened, materials listed, signed')
print('deploy gate: provenance VALID -> proceed')

title: Memory-safe languages as integrity
description: Memory corruption undermines every integrity mechanism above it — a hijacked process attests lies. Memory-safe languages (Rust, Go, Java) remove the corruption class entirely, making higher-level integrity proofs meaningful. Integrity starts with memory safety.
method: Write in memory-safe languages; minimize unsafe; the integrity stack rests on a sound foundation.
usage: Default to memory-safe languages for integrity-critical components.

demo.code:
print('component in safe Rust: no buffer overflow possible')
print('attestation above it: MEANINGFUL (not undermined)')

title: Continuous integrity monitoring
description: Integrity isn't proved once: runtime monitors (IMA in Linux measuring file hashes into the TPM, eBPF integrity watchers) continuously verify that running code still matches the attested measurements. Drift triggers alerts — integrity as an ongoing property, not a boot-time event.
method: Measure at load (IMA); monitor at runtime (eBPF); compare against allowlisted measurements; alert on divergence.
usage: Enforce IMA policies; watch critical binaries at runtime; investigate every divergence.

demo.code:
print('IMA: /usr/bin/authd hash matches policy')
print('eBPF: text segment modified at runtime -> ALERT (injection?)')

title: Sigstore signing and verification
description: Sigstore makes code signing usable: short-lived certificates bound to OIDC identity, signatures and transparency-log entries for every artifact. 'cosign verify' checks who built an artifact and that it's logged — signing without key management pain.
method: Sign artifacts with Sigstore (Fulcio + Rekor); verify identity, signature, and log inclusion on consume.
usage: Sign every release artifact; verify in deployment pipelines; pin identities.

demo.code:
print('cosign sign artifact.tar.gz -> Rekor entry #8812001')
print('deploy: verify identity builder@ci + Rekor inclusion -> OK')

title: Reproducible builds as integrity
description: If anyone can rebuild the binary bit-identically from source, integrity reduces to source review: the binary can't hide what the source doesn't show. Reproducible builds plus source audit is integrity without trusting the build machine — the open-source supply-chain defense.
method: Reproducible build pipeline; independent rebuilders; compare hashes; publish the consensus.
usage: Make builds reproducible; run independent rebuilders; alert on mismatch.

demo.code:
print('3 independent rebuilders: hashes a1b2, a1b2, a1b2')
print('consensus: binary matches source -> INTEGRITY')
